exceptions.reason: The tree is instanced once, in NativeOnInitialized; a control already holding its parts cannot be handed a different hierarchy without throwing away every behaviour and binding wired onto the old one. Set it on the archetype, or on a control that has not initialized yet.

FVirtualKeyboardOptions is a plain USTRUCT in Slate (IVirtualKeyboardEntry.h) with no BlueprintType on it, so UHT rejects both a BlueprintReadWrite property of that type and a BlueprintCallable accessor taking one. UMG's own UEditableTextBox carries it the same way, EditAnywhere with no Blueprint access. The designer, .dui and C++ all reach it: UDreamTextInput::SetVirtualKeyboardOptions pushes it to UUITextInput.

A BlueprintSetter has to take the property's own type, and TWeakObjectPtr<UUIScrollbar> is not something a UFUNCTION parameter can be. SetScrollbar(UUIScrollbar*) is the Blueprint road: it takes the raw pointer a caller actually has, moves the value-changed subscription off the old bar and re-syncs the new one, which a plain variable write would skip.

The property is TArray<TObjectPtr<UObject>>, which a UFUNCTION parameter cannot be, so no BlueprintSetter can match its type. SetItemObjects(const TArray<UObject*>&) is the BlueprintCallable road and is what every caller already uses: it settles the selection and the subclass index-keyed state against the outgoing source before rebuilding the rows.

TArray<TObjectPtr<UObject>> again, for the same reason as UDreamListViewBase::ItemObjects: a BlueprintSetter has to take the property's own type and a UFUNCTION parameter cannot be that one. SetRootItems(const TArray<UObject*>&) is the Blueprint road and re-walks the hierarchy, which a plain variable write would skip.
